expectations.text: both-keys-declared-in-keys: {t}:leases and {t}:due are both passed in KEYS, not constructed inside the script body
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:32-33 `local LEASES = KEYS[1]` / `local DUE = KEYS[2]`; no string concatenation of key names anywhere. DESIGN.md:10 `EVALSHA <sha> 2 {t}:leases {t}:due`. Verified live: script loaded and ran with numkeys=2 on df-v1.34.0.

expectations.text: single-hmget-for-batch: the batch of up to 64 lease fields is read with one HMGET rather than per-item HGET
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:63 `local stored = rcall('HMGET', LEASES, table.unpack(ids, 1, n))` — the only read; the decision loop (68-92) issues no calls.

expectations.text: batched-hset-and-zadd-for-successes: successful renewals are written with one multi-field HSET and one multi-member ZADD (or equivalent single batched calls)
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:94-98 `acall('HSET', LEASES, table.unpack(hset, 1, hn))` and `acall('ZADD', DUE, table.unpack(zadd, 1, zn))`, guarded by `if hn > 0`. Live run with 4 items produced the expected hash and zset state.

expectations.text: explicit-64-bound-and-chunking-awareness: the script enforces an explicit bound of 64 items and shows awareness of unpack/argument-count chunking limits
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:35,48-50 `MAX_ITEMS = 64` with hard rejection of n > 64. DESIGN.md:126-128 'No unbounded unpack. The largest splice is ZADD with 2x64 = 128 arguments, far under the measured Lua ceiling (8163 fields unpack, 8164 is a stack overflow) ... if the cap were ever raised past ~1000, chunk HMGET/HSET/ZADD at 256-1000'.

expectations.text: per-item-status-stable-protocol: the reply carries a per-item status covering renewed/token_mismatch/expired/missing with a stable constant-arity protocol
expectations.evidence: DESIGN.md:51-65 flat array of arity exactly 1+2n, positional, integer status codes 1/2/3/0 plus a deadline string per item; rationale for constant arity given ('a Lua array reply truncates at the first nil'). Live: `1789529624005 1 <deadline> 2 9999999999999 3 1 0 0` for renew/mismatch/expired/missing.

expectations.text: server-time-used-for-deadline: the new deadline is computed from server time obtained on the server, per the stated contract
expectations.evidence: renew_leases_batch.lua:55-57 `local t = rcall('TIME')` -> `now_ms` -> `new_deadline = now_ms + ttl_ms`; no caller clock in ARGV. DESIGN.md:210-212 rejects caller-supplied now_ms explicitly.

expectations.text: measurement-plan-names-script-latency-and-equal-seed: the verification note names SCRIPT LATENCY or the eval coordination counters, an identical-seed comparison, and p50 plus p99
expectations.evidence: DESIGN.md:163-167 eval_io_coordination_total / eval_shardlocal_coordination_total delta per invocation; :178-182 `scripts/script_latency.py --sha <sha> --watch` (SCRIPT LATENCY, with the cumulative-histogram caveat); :168-174 `--reseed --compare naive.lua renew_leases_batch.lua` on identical seeded state with byte-identical reply assertion; :173 'Report p50 and p99'.

expectations.text: no-unverified-redis-only-advice: the design contains no Redis-origin performance advice presented without Dragonfly evidence
expectations.evidence: Dragonfly-specific claims are each tied to evidence: DESIGN.md:93-98 'measured on df-v1.34.0 ... one invocation moves eval_io_coordination_total by +1' and the explicit correction 'A shared {hashtag} does not by itself co-locate keys on default flags - only --lock_on_hashtags'; :110-112 uses the Dragonfly `--!df flags=` syntax and notes `no-writes` is parsed and ignored; :116 no SCRIPT KILL / no BUSY (a Dragonfly-specific fact, not Redis lore); :192-205 smoke numbers labelled as server-side SCRIPT LATENCY on df-v1.34.0 and explicitly not a shipping number. No FUNCTION, `#!lua` shebang, setresp(3), disable-atomicity-for-speed, or client-pipelining-as-fix advice.
